terms.comment: Classically contubernium is the sharing of a tent, or the squad that shares one (Lewis & Short); Traupman widens it to the soldiers’ quarters. A permanent camp was castra statīva (Lewis & Short s.v. statīvus).

sources: Lewis & Short: contubernium · Lewis & Short: stativus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 185, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
